messages:
Alec: Quick check — I'm mapping 'penalty escape' behavior for the policy engine. We need a clear compat surface: when a route's penalty exceeds a threshold, should the runtime perform a unilateral fallback (fast, opaque) or always ask the policy broker for an explicit hard-fallback decision?

Marta: +1 to formalize. Runtime doing silent hard swaps makes audits and billing weird. We should define two behaviors: a low-cost local 'soft escape' and a broker-driven 'hard escape'.

Cheng: Tradeoff: broker round-trip adds ~5-20ms p99 depending on region. For very latency-sensitive routes, local soft escapes are valuable. But soft escapes can cause subtle correctness drift if the runtime picks an incompatible model variant.

Samir: Proposal: add a small RouteBinding flag `allow_local_escape` (default false) and separate TTL for soft escapes. If set, runtime can apply soft escape heuristics within a constrained window.

Alec: Sketching DSL:
```
route "chat-gen" {
  soft_escape { 
    enabled = true
    penalty_threshold = 0.7
    multiplier = 1.15
    max_retries = 2
    ttl = "30s"
  }
  hard_escape {
    enabled = true
    broker_signal = "fallback_request"
  }
}
```
This keeps runtime behavior explicit and observable.

Marta: That looks good. We also need a clear policy-broker contract for hard_escape so brokers can return: `accept_swap`, `defer`, or `force-route: <route-id>`. Keep the error model deterministic.

Cheng: For telemetry, we should emit metrics: `route.escape.soft.count`, `route.escape.hard.request.count`, `route.escape.hard.latency_ms`, and tags for tenant/region/route_id. Those let us quantify cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Samir: Also need a compatibility matrix: which model variants are eligible for soft_swap. Runtime should check `compatibility_score >= X` before soft-swapping, otherwise escalate to broker.

Alec: Good catch. Add `compatibility_requirements` to the route binding and a cheap local checker in the runtime. If failed, runtime must do hard_escape.

Marta: Offline sim obligations: prod-sim-bot should run sim with both behaviors (soft-first and broker-first) and diff outcomes on latency, cost, and correctness.

prod-sim-bot: Sim job queued: `sim/penalty-escape-2026-03` — estimated 6h. Will post results to #eng-sim-results.

Cheng: On the runtime side, implement opt-in flags to avoid global rollouts: `--enable-soft-escape` and `--soft-escape-strictness=low|medium|high`. Start conservative.

Samir: Operationally, we need a recovery story: if soft-escape causes a regression, telemetry should trigger auto-disable for that tenant-route for X minutes and open a ticket. Ops-bot can create an incident or alert.

ops-bot: Alert rule created: `RouteSoftEscapeAnomaly` (severity: P2) — triggers if correctness-regression > 0.5% over 15m.

Alec: Action items: (1) I will draft a small RFC describing DSL and broker response schema, (2) Cheng will prototype runtime flags and local compatibility checker, (3) Marta will add sim cases and expected metrics, (4) Samir will add migration notes for Dedicated customers.

Marta: Timeline: RFC in 2 days, runtime prototype in 1 week, sim results + decision in ~10 days.

Cheng: Fine by me. I'll also add a simple perf harness to measure the broker RTT impact by region.

Samir: If we keep the escape contract small and observable, we should be able to iterate without tenant surprises. :+1:

Alec: Thanks all — will drop RFC link here when ready.
